source: Based on a modified version of the PhiUSIIL Phishing URL dataset (Prasad and Chandra, 2024, UCI, CC BY 4.0): duplicate links removed and the label recoded.
dataset_note: In this dataset every legitimate link is a website's homepage, such as https://www.example.com, with nothing after the name. Real links to safe sites are often longer, so these charts show warning signs, not proof that a link is safe.

charts.title: How many links are phishing and how many are legitimate
charts.takeaway: About 43% of links are phishing and 57% are legitimate, so the dataset is mildly imbalanced.

charts.title: Links that use HTTPS (the padlock)
charts.takeaway: About 49% of phishing links use HTTPS too, so a padlock does not mean a link is safe.

charts.title: Links longer than 50 characters
charts.takeaway: About 22% of phishing links are longer than 50 characters. A long, messy link is a warning sign, but a short link is not proof that it is safe.

charts.title: Links that contain a hyphen (-)
charts.takeaway: About 36% of phishing links contain a hyphen, against 7% of legitimate ones. Fake sites often join words with hyphens to look like a real company's name.
